title: FlattenOptions.gAvroParity() joins array element fields with a single separator, exactly as GAvroSchemaFlattener does
rationale: The second axis of parity, isolated on an underscore-free schema so the boundary marker is the only variable, and the positive twin of enriched-gavro-parity-claim-fails-at-array-boundaries. The correction that made this row possible is worth stating: GAvroSchemaFlattener has no array-boundary marker at all. Its useArrayBoundarySeparator flag globally renames the ONE separator from _ to __, so its default emits a single _ at an array boundary and its non-default emits __ everywhere. The enriched model - a separator plus a distinct boundary marker - corresponds to NEITHER GAvro configuration, which is why parity has to set the boundary separator equal to the separator rather than to either GAvro value.
catchesBugClass: gAvroParity() acquiring a boundary marker, or GAvro's default changing. Together with its twin it also catches the whole repair being reverted: if the factory collapsed back into the defaults, this row would go red and the twin would stay green, which is the asymmetry that tells a reader which of the two configurations moved.
cannotCatch: It cannot reach the doubled-separator recipe gAvroParity()'s javadoc publishes for callers who ran GAvro with useArrayBoundarySeparator(true); the unit test theDocumentedDoubledSeparatorRecipeMatchesGAvroWithUseArrayBoundarySeparator executes that, because minting a second factory for a mode the manifest classifies as a misnamed control would advertise it. It also cannot see an array of arrays of records, where the two flatteners genuinely diverge and no option closes the gap.

predicted.detail: Both arms render [items_sku]. The enriched defaults render items__sku on this same schema, which is what the DEFECT twin records.

configDescription: assert ENRICHED_KEYSET vs GAVRO_SCHEMA_FLATTENER, preset GAVRO_PARITY
